title: Pad Kra Pao (Thai Basil Pork Stir-Fry)
summary: Minced pork stir-fried in a charcoal-fired wok with pounded garlic and red chilies, seasoned with dark soy, oyster sauce and fish sauce, then finished with Thai basil and served over rice under a fried egg. He gives no quantities at any point.

ingredients.note: Spoken as "a little bit of yum-yum" at 0:37 while he holds a small red sachet up to camera; the label is never legible, so whether it is MSG or a branded seasoning is unconfirmed.

steps.text: Pound the garlic cloves and red chilies to a rough paste in a granite mortar.
Set the wok over a very hot charcoal fire and add oil.
Fry the pounded chili and garlic in the oil until it smells cooked and fragrant.
Add the minced pork and stir-fry, breaking it up, until it starts to brown.
Season with dark soy sauce, oyster sauce and fish sauce, stirring each one through.
Add sugar and stir it through.
Add a little of the seasoning powder ("yum-yum").
Add the Thai basil and toss it through the pork.
Add a bit more oil, give it a final toss and take it off the heat.
Spoon the pork over cooked white rice.
Top with a fried egg, yolk still runny.

notes: He gives no quantities anywhere in the video and there are no on-screen quantity cards, so every amount is left to taste. A 117-frame OCR sweep at 0.5 s steps found no overlay text at all.
His caption prefers a mix of Thai basil and holy basil; the video itself says "add our Thai basil" at 0:41.
Cooked outdoors in a well-seasoned wok on a charcoal brazier, with the wok tossed over open flame late in the cook — a domestic hob will need the wok preheated hard instead.
The caption's opinions ("should have used Italian basil", the pork tasting better in Australia) are the creator's own, not something the video demonstrates.
gaps: No quantities are given for any ingredient — not spoken, on screen, or in the caption.
The fried egg is only shown already cooked, being placed on the plate at 0:57; how he fries it is not shown.
The rice appears already cooked on the plate; the video never shows it being cooked.
The "yum-yum" seasoning sachet is never legible, so the product is unidentified.

source.quantity_basis: Nothing quantified: the voiceover names ingredients only, the caption lists none, and OCR over 117 frames found zero on-screen text. Ingredient identities come from the local ASR transcript and the frames; every amount is therefore null with basis "unstated".
